line: Jung's statements on the five: the fifth as the unity of the four, the quintessence of the alchemists, and the rotundum as fifth stage.

sections.title: The fifth and the four
sections.line: CW9ii ¶ 350 and ¶ 427: the fifth as the unity of the four, and the rotundum at the fifth stage.

quotes.quote: The inhabitant, in his turn, has a relationship to the quaternity, and to the fifth as the unity of the four.
As the fifth stage, the rotundum would then be identical with the first; that is to say, the heavy darkness of the earth, metal, has a secret relationship to the Anthropos.

sections.title: The quintessence
sections.line: CW14 ¶ 187 and ¶ 354 and ¶ 429: the arcane substance, the cauda pavonis and the Maid in the fifth circle.

quotes.quote: It is a symbol of the arcane substance and the quintessence, of the aether that contains all four elements, and at the same time a God-image or, to be more accurate, an image of the anima mundi.
The cauda pavonis is also called the “soul of the world, nature, the quintessence, which causes all things to bring forth.”
The elements are evidently conceived as circles, for the Quinta Essentia, the “Maid,” appears in the fifth.
